Then $X$ is a hyperbolic metric space if and only if a flaring condition is satisfied.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\cite[Proposition 5.17]{pranab-mahan}
	Let $K=\pi_1(S^h)$ be the fundamental group of a surface with finitely many punctures and let $K_1,\ldots,K_n$ be its peripheral subgroups. Let $1\to K\to G\stackrel{\pi}{\to} Q\to1$ and $1\to K_i\to N_G(K_i)\stackrel{\pi}{\to}Q_i\to 1$ be the induced short exact sequences of groups. Then $G$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to $\{N_G(K_i)\}^n_{i=1}$ if and only if $Q$ is a convex cocompact subgroup of the pure mapping class group of $S^h$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{weak comb}
Let $\pi:X\rightarrow B$ be an $\eta$-metric (graph) bundle such that \begin{enumerate}
	\item[(C1)] $B$ is a $\delta_0$-hyperbolic metric space.
	\item[(C2)] For each $b\in V(B)$, the fiber $F_b$ strongly hyperbolic relative to a collection of uniformly mutually cobounded subsets ${\mathcal H}_b$.
	\item[(C3)] For each $b\in V(B)$, the barycentre map $\partial^3\widehat{F}_b\to \widehat{F}_b$ is coarsely $N$-surjective.	
	\item[(C4)] The induced coned-off metric (graph) bundle satisfies the $(\nu_k, M_k,n_k)$-flaring condition, for each $k\geq 1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $X$ is weakly hyperbolic relative to ${\mathcal C}$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Recall that $\mathcal{X}$ is a metric graph bundle over the hyperbolic base space $B$ with $\delta_0$-hyperbolic fibers $\widehat{F}_b$ for each $b\in V(B)$. Then along with conditions (C3) and (C4), $\mathcal{X}$ satisfies all the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{mbdl thm}. Therefore, $\mathcal{X}$ is a hyperbolic metric space. \\
Now, ${\mathcal B}$ is a collection of uniformly separated, uniformly quasiconvex subsets of $\mathcal{X}$. Therefore, by Lemma~\ref{coned-off hyp}, ${\mathcal E}(\mathcal{X},{\mathcal B})$ is a hyperbolic metric space. Therefore, $(\mathcal{X},{\mathcal B})$ is weakly relatively hyperbolic.  By Remark \ref{coned off-pel qi}, ${\mathcal E}(\mathcal{X},{\mathcal B})$ is is quasiisometric to ${\mathcal E}(X,{\mathcal C})$ and thus, ${\mathcal E}(X,{\mathcal C})$ is a hyperbolic metric space. Therefore, $X$ is weakly hyperbolic relative to ${\mathcal C}$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{cone flare implies bcp}
	Suppose the metric (graph) bundle $\mathcal{X}$ is hyperbolic and it satisfies a cone-bounded strictly flare condition. Then there exists $D>0$ such that ${\mathcal B}$ is a mutually $D$-cobounded collection of subsets.
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Suppose not. Then for every $D\geq D_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$, there exists ${\mathcal B}_\alpha,{\mathcal B}_\beta\in{\mathcal B}$, $x,y\in {\mathcal B}_{\alpha}$ and their nearest point projections $x_1,y_1\in {\mathcal B}_\beta$ respectively such that $d(x_1,y_1)\geq D$. Then by Lemma~\ref{big npp small nbd}, $[x_1,y_1]\subset N^{\mathcal{X}}_{M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}}([x,y])$. Let $x_2,y_2\in[x,y]$ such that $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x_1,x_2)\leq M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}},d_{\mathcal{X}}(y_1,y_2)\leq M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$. Clearly, $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x_2,y_2)\geq d_{\mathcal{X}}(x_1,y_1)-d_{\mathcal{X}}(x_1,x_2)-d_{\mathcal{X}}(y_1,y_2)\geq D-2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$. For $i=1,2$, let $\gamma_i=[x_i,y_i]$.

Consider $\pi(\gamma_i)$ in $B$ for $i=1,2$. Since each ${\mathcal B}_\alpha\in{\mathcal B}$ is an isometric embedding of $B$ in $\mathcal{X}$, $d_B(\pi(x_i),\pi(y_i))\geq D-2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$ and moreover, $d_B(\pi(x_1),\pi(x_2))\leq M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}, d_B(\pi(y_1),\pi(y_2))\leq M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$. Let $x_0,y_0$ denote the lifts of $\pi(x_1),\pi(y_1)$ in ${\mathcal B}_\alpha$. Then $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x_1,x_0)\leq d_{\mathcal{X}}(x_1,x_2)+d_{\mathcal{X}}(x_2,x_0)=d_{\mathcal{X}}(x_1,x_2)+d_B(\pi(x_2),\pi(x_1))\leq 2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$. Similarly, $d_{\mathcal{X}}(y_1,y_0)\leq 2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$. Note that the geodesic $\gamma_0:=[x_0,y_0]$ in ${\mathcal B}_\alpha$ has length at least $D-2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$.\\
So, we have geodesics $\gamma_0\subset{\mathcal B}_{\alpha},\gamma_1\subset{\mathcal B}_\beta$ of length at least $D-2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}$ such that $\pi(x_1)=\pi(x_0)$ and $\pi(y_1)=\pi(y_0)$. $Hd_{\mathcal{X}}(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)\leq 2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}+2\delta$, where $\delta$ is the hyperbolicity constant of $\mathcal{X}$. So, for each $x'\in\gamma_1$, there exists $y'\in\gamma_0$ such that $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x',y')\leq 2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}+2\delta$. Since $d_{B}(\pi(x'),\pi(y'))\leq 2M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}+2\delta$, there exists $y''\in\gamma_0$ with $\pi(y'')=\pi(y')$ such that $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x',y'')\leq 4(M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}+\delta)$ and thus, $d_{\widehat{F}_{\pi(x)}}(x',y'')\leq\eta_{\ref{new mbdl}}(4(M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}+\delta))=:M_1$. So, there exists a cone-bounded hallway $f:[-m,m]\times [0,1]\to\mathcal{X}$ of length $2m\geq D-4(M_{\ref{big npp small nbd}}+\delta)$ with $f([-m,m]\times\{0\})=\gamma_1$, $f([-m,m]\times\{1\})=\gamma_0$ satisfying 
$$l(f(\{i\}\times[0,1]))\leq M_1, \text{ for } -m\leq i\leq m.$$
As we increase $D$, $m$ also increases, but $M_1$ is fixed. Thus, for every $\lambda>1$, there exists a cone-bounded hallway which does not flare, violating the cone-bounded hallway strictly flare condition.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{strong comb}
	Let $\pi:X\rightarrow B$ be an $\eta$-metric (graph) bundle such that \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=\parindent,align=left,labelwidth=\parindent,labelsep=0pt]
		\item[(C1) ] $B$ is a $\delta_0$-hyperbolic metric space.
		\item[(C2) ] Each fiber $F_b$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to a collection of uniformly mutually cobounded subsets ${\mathcal H}_b$.
		\item[(C3) ] For each fiber, the barycentre map $\partial^3\widehat{F}_b\to \widehat{F}_b$ is coarsely $N$-surjective.	
		\item[(C4) ] The induced coned-off metric graph bundle satisfies the $(\nu_k, M_k,n_k)$-flaring condition, for each $k\geq 1$.
		\item[(C5) ] The cone bounded strictly flare condition is satisfied.
	\end{enumerate}
	Then $X$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to ${\mathcal C}$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{weak comb} and Lemma~\ref{cone flare implies bcp}, we have that $\mathcal{X}$ is a hyperbolic metric space and ${\mathcal B}$ are mutually $D$-cobounded subsets of $\mathcal{X}$. Then, by Lemma~\ref{coned-off strong hyp}, $(\mathcal{X},{\mathcal B})$ is strongly relatively hyperbolic. Equivalently, $(X,{\mathcal C})$ is also strongly relatively hyperbolic.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{Combination converse}
Let $\pi:X\rightarrow B$ be an $\eta$-metric (graph) bundle such that \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=\parindent,align=left,labelwidth=\parindent,labelsep=4pt]
	\item[(C1)] $B$ is a $\delta_0$-hyperbolic metric space.
	\item[(C2)] For each $b\in V(B)$, the fiber $F_b$ strongly hyperbolic relative to a collection of uniformly separated closed subsets ${\mathcal H}_b$.
	\item[(C3)] For each $b\in V(B)$, the barycentre map $\partial^3\widehat{F}_b\to \widehat{F}_b$ is coarsely $N$-surjective.	
\end{enumerate}
If $(X,{\mathcal C})$ is strongly relatively hyperbolic, then the induced coned-off metric (graph) bundle satisfies a flaring condition and a cone bounded strictly flare condition.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Since $(X,{\mathcal C})$ is strongly relatively hyperbolic, by Lemma~\ref{brahma-amalgeo}, ${\mathcal P}{\mathcal E}(X,{\mathcal C},{\mathcal B},{\mathcal G})=\mathcal{X}$ is a hyperbolic metric space with ${\mathcal B}$, is a collection of quasiconvex subsets of ${\mathcal P}{\mathcal E}(X,{\mathcal C},{\mathcal B},{\mathcal G})$. This, along with the conditions (C1),(C2),(C3) and Theorem~\ref{mbdl thm}, we have that $\mathcal{X}$ satisfies a flaring condition. \\
Now we will show that cone-bounded flaring condition is satisfied. Suppose not. Then there exists some $k\geq 1$ and $M\geq 1$ such that for all $n>0$, we have the following. Let $\gamma:[-n,n]\rightarrow B$ be a geodesic with $k$-qi lifts
$\tilde{\gamma}_1$ and $\tilde{\gamma}_2$ lying in the cone locus ${\mathcal B}_{\alpha}$ and ${\mathcal B}_{\beta}$ respectively satisfying $$d_{\gamma(i)}(\tilde{\gamma}_1(i),\tilde{\gamma}_2(i))\leq M \text{ for all } i\in[-n,n].$$ Let $\mu$ be an electric geodesic in $\widehat{F}_{\gamma(-n)}$ joining $\tilde{\gamma}_1(-n)$ and $\tilde{\gamma}_2(-n)$. Similarly, let $\mu'$ be an electric geodesic in $\widehat{F}_{\gamma(n)}$ joining $\tilde{\gamma}_1(n)$ and $\tilde{\gamma}_2(n)$. Then length of $\mu$ in $\widehat{F}_{\gamma(-n)}$ and that of $\mu'$ in $\widehat{F}_{\gamma(n)}$ is at most $M$. Let $a=\mu\cap{\mathcal C}_{\alpha}$ and $a'=\mu'\cap{\mathcal C}_{\alpha}$.

Let $\sigma_1$ be a concatenation of the edge $[a,\tilde{\gamma}_1(-n)]$, $\tilde{\gamma}_1$ and the edge $[\tilde{\gamma}_1(n),a']$. Let $\sigma_2$ be the concatenation of $\mu|_{[a,\tilde{\gamma}_2(-n)]}$, $\tilde{\gamma}_2$ and $\mu'|_{[\tilde{\gamma}_2(n),a']}$. Since $M$ is fixed, by Lemma \ref{extend quasigeodesic}, both $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ are partially electrocuted quasigeodesics in $\mathcal{X}$. The paths $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$ pass through different elements of ${\mathcal B}$ for $2n$ distance. As $n$ can be arbitrarily large, we get a contradiction to the similar intersection pattern.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{CT for mgbdl}\cite[Theorem 5.2]{krishna-sardar}
Suppose $X$ is a metric (graph) bundle over a hyperbolic metric space $B$ such that $X$ is hyperbolic and all the fibers are nonelementary uniformly hyperbolic, and the barycenter map is uniformly coarsely surjective. Suppose $i:A\rightarrow B$ is a Lipschitz, qi embedding 
and $Y$ is the pullback of $X$ under $i$. Then $Y$ is hyperbolic and $f:Y\to X$ admits the CT map.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{type preserving bundle morphism}
The metric graph bundle $(X,B,\pi)$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to ${\mathcal C}=\{\psi_X({\mathcal C}'_{\alpha})\mid{\mathcal C}'_{\alpha}\in{\mathcal C}'\}$.
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
We can easily check that $(X,B,\pi)$ satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{strong comb}. (C1) is obvious and (C2) holds by Proposition~\ref{approx bundle rel hyp} and Lemma~\ref{for mg approx}. Similarly, (C3) also holds. Finally (C4) and (C5) follow from the assumptions. Thus, $X$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to ${\mathcal C}$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{induced qi bundle}
	The map $\psi^h:X'^h\to X^h$ induced by $\psi$ is a  quasiisometry.
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
\label{about coned-off Y}
$(1)$ Note that the pullback map $f$ is type preserving by Proposition~\ref{pullback}. So for each $b\in V(A)$, the collection of horosphere-like subsets of $F_b$ is identified with ${\mathcal H}_{i(b)}\subset F_{i(b)}$. Let ${\mathcal H}_Y=\{{\mathcal H}_{i(b)}\}_{b\in V(A)}$.\\
$(2)$ ${\mathcal C}_Y$ is a collection of subgraphs ${\mathcal C}_{Y,\alpha}$ of $Y$ where $V({\mathcal C}_{Y,\alpha})$ is the disjoint union of vertex sets of the horosphere-like subsets of the fibers of $Y$. Moreover, any two such vertices are joined by an edge in ${\mathcal C}_Y$ if they are joined by an edge in $Y$. So each ${\mathcal C}_{Y,\alpha}$ can be identified with ${\mathcal C}_\alpha\cap Y$.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- lemma-42: body_md -->
\label{rel hyp of Y}
The metric graph bundle $(Y,A,p)$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to a collection of subsets ${\mathcal C}_Y$.
<!-- end lemma-42 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{pullback}, $(Y,A,p)$ is a relatively hyperbolic metric graph bundle. Note that $A$ is a hyperbolic metric space. The space $\mathcal{Y}$ is obtained as in Proposition~\ref{new mbdl}. Hyperbolicity of $\mathcal{Y}$ follows from Theorem~\ref{CT for mgbdl}. 
Since each fiber $F_b$ in $Y$, $b\in V(A)$, is isometric to the fiber $F_{i(b)}$ in $X$, $F_b$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to a collection of subsets ${\mathcal H}_b$. Moreover, the barycenter map $\partial^3\widehat{F}_b\to F_b$ is uniformly coarsely surjective since the barycenter map of $F_{i(b)}$ is coarsely surjective. By \cite[Remark 4.4]{pranab-mahan} and bounded flaring condition, ${\mathcal E}(Y,{\mathcal H}_Y)$ inherits the flaring condition of ${\mathcal E}(X,{\mathcal H})$ and similarly, $(Y,{\mathcal H}_Y)$ inherits the cone-bounded strictly flare condition of $(X,{\mathcal H})$. By Theorem~\ref{mbdl thm}, this completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{coned-off pullback}
	Suppose $\pi:X\rightarrow B$ is a metric (graph) bundle satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{main theorem}. Let $i: A\rightarrow B$ is a Lipschitz $k$-qi embedding and $p:Y\rightarrow A$ be the pullback bundle with the pullback map $f:Y\rightarrow X$. Then $\mathcal{Y}$ is a pullback of $\mathcal{X}$.
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- lemma-43: body_md -->
\label{prop-embed}\cite[Lemma 5.20]{krishna-sardar}
	The pullback of a metric (graph) bundle is metrically properly embedded in it.
<!-- end lemma-43 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{ladder subdivision}\cite[Corollary 5.10]{krishna-sardar} There exists constants $R_0>0, R_1, R'_1, D_1$ and there is a partition $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots <t_n=l$ of $[0,l]$ and $K_1$-qi sections ${\Sigma}_i$ passing through $\alpha(t_i)$, $0\leq i\leq n$ inside ${\mathbb L}({\Sigma}, {\Sigma}')$ such that the following holds.\\
	$(1)$ ${\Sigma}_0={\Sigma}, {\Sigma}_n={\Sigma}'$.\\
	$(2)$ For $0\leq i\leq n-2$, ${\Sigma}_{i+1}\subset {\mathbb L}({\Sigma}_i, {\Sigma}')$.\\
	$(3)$ For $0\leq i\leq n-2$, there are two possibilities. $(\textup{I})$ $d_h({\Sigma}_i, {\Sigma}_{i+1})=R_0$,\\
	$(\textup{II})$ $d_h({\Sigma}_i, {\Sigma}_{i+1})>R_0$ and there is a $K_2$-qi section ${\Sigma}'_i$ through $\alpha(t_{i+1}-1)$ inside ${\mathbb L}({\Sigma}_i, {\Sigma}_{i+1})$ such that $d_h({\Sigma}_i, {\Sigma}'_i)<R_1$.		
		In either case $d_X({\Sigma}_i, {\Sigma}_{i+1})>R'_1$ and ${\Sigma}_i, {\Sigma}_{i+1}$ are $D_1$-cobounded in $\mathcal{X}$.\\
	$(4)$ $d_h({\Sigma}_{n-1}, {\Sigma}_n)\leq R_0$.
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- lemma-44: body_md -->
\cite[Lemmas 5.12,5.18, Proposition 2.38]{krishna-sardar}\label{main quasigeodesics}
	There exists $K_{\ref{main quasigeodesics}}\geq1$ such that the path $c(y,y')$ (resp. $\bar{c}(y,y')$) is a $K_{\ref{main quasigeodesics}}$-quasigeodesic in $\mathcal{X}$ (resp. $\mathcal{Y}$).
<!-- end lemma-44 -->
<!-- lemma-45: body_md -->
\label{vertical qg}
There exists $K_{\ref{vertical qg}}\geq 1$ such that for any $x\in{\mathbb L}\cap X$, there exists a vertical quasigeodesic ray $r_x:V([\pi(x),b_0])\to X$ such that $r_x(\pi(x))=x$ and $d_B(\pi(x),v)\leq d_X(r_x(\pi(x)),r_x(v))\leq K_{\ref{vertical qg}}d_B(\pi(x),v)$.
<!-- end lemma-45 -->
<!-- lemma-46: body_md -->
\label{criterion satisfied}\cite[Lemma 5.21]{krishna-sardar}
	Given $D>0$, there is $D_{\ref{criterion satisfied}}>0$ such that the following holds.		
	If $d_{\mathcal{X}}(y_0,c)\leq D$ then $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(y_0,\bar{c})\leq D_{\ref{criterion satisfied}}$.
<!-- end lemma-46 -->
<!-- lemma-47: body_md -->
\label{criterion satisfied-2}
	Given $D>0$, there is $D_{\ref{criterion satisfied-2}}=D_{\ref{criterion satisfied-2}}(D)>0$ such that the following holds.	
	If $d_{X}(y_0,c\cap X)\leq D$ then $d_{Y}(y_0,\bar{c}\cap Y)\leq D_{\ref{criterion satisfied-2}}$.
<!-- end lemma-47 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Let $x\in c\cap X$ such that $d_X(y_0,x)\leq D$. Then we have, $d_{\mathcal{X}}(y_0,x)\leq D$. 
	
	\noindent	
	Recall that $c$ is a concatenation of lift of geodesic segments of $B$ in  $K_2$-qi section ${\Sigma}_k$ or ${\Sigma}'_k$ and fiber geodesics. Let ${\mathcal Q},{\mathcal Q}'$ be consecutive $K_2$-qi sections with $d_h({\mathcal Q},{\mathcal Q}')\leq R_0$ and $x\in{\mathbb L}({\mathcal Q},{\mathcal Q}')$. Then $c\cap{\mathbb L}({\mathcal Q},{\mathcal Q}')$ is either a lift of a geodesic segment of $B$ in ${\mathcal Q}$, joining the points $z$ to $w$ or it is the concatenation of this lift and a fiber geodesic $\sigma$ in $\widehat{F}_{\pi(w)}$ joining ${\mathcal Q}$ to ${\mathcal Q}'$. Let $z'={\mathcal Q}'\cap\sigma$ and $b'=\pi(z')$. Note that $z$ and $z'$ are one of the $y_k$'s or $y'_k$'s. 
	
	So we have two cases. First, suppose $x\in\sigma\cap X$. Let $b$ be a nearest point projection of $\pi(x)$ on $A$. Then, $d_B(\pi(x),b)\leq d_B(\pi(x),b_0)\leq D$. By the definition of $\bar{c}$, ${\mathbb L}({\mathcal Q},{\mathcal Q}')\cap F_{b}\subset\bar{c}$. By Lemma \ref{vertical qg}, there exists $y\in{\mathbb L}({\mathcal Q},{\mathcal Q}')\cap F_b$ such that $d_X(x,y)\leq K_{\ref{vertical qg}}d_B(\pi(x),\pi(y))\leq K_{\ref{vertical qg}}D$. 
	
	Now suppose $x$ lies in the lift of the geodesic segment $[\pi(z),\pi(w)]_B$ in ${\mathcal Q}$. So, $\pi(x)\in[\pi(z),\pi(w)]_B$. Let $\overline{\pi(z)},\overline{\pi(w)}$ denote the nearest point projections of $\pi(z),\pi(w)$ respectively on $A$. By Lemma~\ref{trivial lemma} and stability of quasigeodesics, 
	$d_B(\pi(x), [\overline{\pi(z)},\overline{\pi(w)}]_A)\leq D_{\ref{trivial lemma}}(D,k_0,\delta)+D_{\ref{stab-qg}}(\delta,k)$. Let $b\in[\overline{\pi(z)},\overline{\pi(w)}]_A$ such that $d_B(\pi(x),b)\leq D_{\ref{trivial lemma}}(D,k_0,\delta)+D_{\ref{stab-qg}}(\delta,k)$. 	
	By the definition of $\bar{c}$, the lift of the geodesic segment $[\overline{\pi(z)},\overline{\pi(w)}]_A$ in ${\mathcal Q}$ is a subsegment of $\bar{c}$. Let $y={\mathcal Q}\cap F_b$. Again by Lemma \ref{vertical qg}, $d_X(x,y)\leq K_{\ref{vertical qg}}d_B(\pi(x),b)\leq K_{\ref{vertical qg}}d_B(\pi(x),b)\leq K_{\ref{vertical qg}}(D_{\ref{trivial lemma}}(D,k_0,\delta)+D_{\ref{stab-qg}}(\delta,k))$.
	
	\noindent
	Let $D_1=\max\{K_{\ref{vertical qg}}D,K_{\ref{vertical qg}}(D_{\ref{trivial lemma}}(D,k_0,\delta)+D_{\ref{stab-qg}}(\delta,k))\}$. Then, $d_X(y_0,y)\leq d_X(y_0,x)+d_X(x,y)\leq D+D_1$. 	
	By Lemma~\ref{prop-embed}, there exists a function $\eta_0:{\mathbb N}\to{\mathbb N}$ such that, $d_Y(y_0,y)\leq\eta_0(D+D_1)$. We take $D_{\ref{criterion satisfied-2}}(D)=\eta_0(D+D_1)$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 3.11]{Pal}\label{pal ct}
Suppose we have a short exact sequence of pairs of finitely generated groups $$1\to (K,K_1)\to (G,N_G(K_1))\stackrel{\pi}{\to} (Q,Q_1)\to1$$ such that $K$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to a non-trivial proper subgroup $K_1$ and $G$ preserves cusps. Moreover, if $G$ is weakly hyperbolic relative to $K_1$ and strongly hyperbolic relative to $N_G(K_1)$, then the embedding $i:\Gamma_K\to\Gamma_G$ admits a CT map.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{combi for short exact seqn}
Let $1\to (K,K_1)\to (G,N_G(K_1))\to (Q,Q_1)\to 1$ be a short exact sequence of pairs of finitely generated groups such that $K$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to a proper non-trivial subgroup $K_1$ and suppose $G$ preserves cusps. Let $G$ be weakly hyperbolic relative to $K_1$ and a cone-bounded strictly flare condition be satisfied by ${\mathcal E}(G,K_1)$. Then $G$ is strongly relatively hyperbolic relative to $N_G(K_1)$.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{main application}
	Suppose $1\to (K,K_1)\to (G,N_G(K_1))\to (Q,Q_1)\to 1$ is a short exact sequence of relatively hyperbolic groups
	where $K$ is strongly hyperbolic relative to a proper non-trivial subgroup $K_1$ and $G$ preserves cusps. Suppose $G$ is weakly hyperbolic relative to $K_1$ and it is strongly hyperbolic relative to $N_G(K_1)$. Suppose $Q'$ is a qi embedded subgroup of $Q$ and $G_1=\pi^{-1}(Q')$.
	Then $(G_1,N_{G_1}(K_1))$ is strongly relatively hyperbolic and $(G_1,N_{G_1}(K_1))\to(G,N_{G}(K_1))$ admits CT.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{bundle boundary}
$\displaystyle{\partial \mathcal{X}=\Lambda\widehat{F}\cup\bigcup_{\xi\in\partial B}\partial^{\xi}\mathcal{X}}$.
<!-- end prop-13 -->
<!-- lemma-48: body_md -->
\label{lemma: ct to base}
	Suppose $b\in B$ and $\alpha_n$ is a sequence of geodesics in $B$ joining $b$ to $b_n$. Let $\tilde{\alpha}_n$ is a uniform qi lift of $\alpha_n$ for all $n$. Suppose $\tilde{\alpha}_n$ joins $\tilde{\alpha}_n(b)=x^0_n$ to $\tilde{\alpha}_n(b_n)=x_n$ and suppose the set $\{x^0_n\}$ has finite diameter. If $x_n\to z\in \partial\mathcal{X}$, then $\lim_{n\to\infty}b_n$
	exists. If $\xi=\lim_{n\to\infty}b_n$ and $\alpha:[0,\infty)\to B$ is a geodesic ray joining $b$ to $\xi$, then there is a uniform qi lift 
	$\tilde{\alpha}$ of $\alpha$ such that $\tilde{\alpha}(\infty)=z$.
<!-- end lemma-48 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Since $x_n\to z$, there exists $D>0$ such that for all $M>0$ there is $N=N(M)>0$ with $Hd_{\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\alpha}_m|_{[0,M]}, \tilde{\alpha}_n|_{[0,M]})\leq D$ for all 
$m,n\geq N$ by Lemma~\ref{lem: bdry defn}(1). Then, for all $M>0$,
$Hd_{B}(\alpha_m|_{[0,M]}, \alpha_n|_{[0,M]})\leq D$ for all $m,n\geq N$. Again by Lemma~\ref{lem: bdry defn}(1), the sequence $\{b_n\}$ converges to a point of $\xi\in\partial B$. Let $\alpha$ be a geodesic ray in $B$ joining $b$ to $\xi$.	We claim that $z\in \partial^{\xi} X$.

Given $t\geq 0$, by Lemma~\ref{lem: bdry defn}(2) there exists $N'=N'(t)$ such that
$d(\alpha(t),\alpha_n)\leq D'$ for all $n\geq N'$, for some $D'$ depending on $\delta$.
Let $N_0=\max\{N(t),N'(t)\}$. Let $t'>0$ be such that $d_X(\alpha(t),\alpha_{N_0}(t'))\leq D'$.
Define $\tilde{\alpha}(t)=\hat{\phi}_{uv}(\tilde{\alpha}_{N_0}(t'))$ where $u=\alpha_{N_0}(t'),v=\alpha(t)$
and $\phi_{uv}$ is a fiber identification map. We can easily see that this defines a qi section over $\alpha$ and $z=\tilde{\alpha}(\infty)$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-49: body_md -->
\label{qi lift in X}
Let $z\in\bigsqcup_{\xi\in\partial B}\partial^{\xi}\mathcal{X}$. Then there exists a qi lift $\tilde{\alpha}$ in $\mathcal{X}$ such that $\tilde{\alpha}\subset X$ and $\tilde{\alpha}(\infty)=z$ in $\partial\mathcal{X}$.
<!-- end lemma-49 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Suppose $z\in\partial^{\xi}\mathcal{X}$ for some $\xi\in\partial B$. Let $\beta$ be geodesic ray $B$ with $\beta(\infty)=\xi$ and let $\tilde{\beta}$ be a qi lift with $\tilde{\beta}(
\infty)=z$. We define a path $\tilde{\alpha}$ as follows. For each $n\in{\mathbb Z}_{\geq0}$, $\tilde{\alpha}(n)=\tilde{\beta}(n)$ if $\tilde{\beta}(n)\in X$. If $\tilde{\beta}(n)\in\nu(H_{b,\alpha})$ for some $H_{b,\alpha}\in{\mathcal H}_b$ for some $b\in V(B)$, then define $\tilde{\alpha}(n)=h$ for some $h\in H_{b,\alpha}$. This is a discrete path satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\alpha},\tilde{\beta})\leq\frac{1}{2}$. Moreover, it is coarsely unique. If for any $n\in{\mathbb Z}_{\geq0}$, $\tilde{\beta}(n)\in\nu(H_{b,\alpha})$ and $\tilde{\alpha}(n)=h$ and if we have another path $\tilde{\alpha'}$ defined as above with $\tilde{\alpha'}(n)=h'$ for some $h'\in H_{b,\alpha}$, then clearly, $d_{\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\alpha},\tilde{\alpha'})\leq 1$. Next we show that $\tilde{\alpha}$ is a quasigeodesic ray. Let $m>n\geq 0$. Then $l_{\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\alpha}([n,m]))=\sum_{i=n}^{m-1}d_{\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\alpha}(i),\tilde{\alpha}(i+1))\leq\sum_{i=n}^{m-1}d_{\mathcal{X}}((\tilde{\beta}(i),\tilde{\beta}(i+1))+1)=2(m-n)\leq 2d_{\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\alpha}(n),\tilde{\alpha}(m))$. Moreover, clearly, $\pi(\tilde{\alpha})=\beta$. Therefore, $\tilde{\alpha}$ is a qi lift with $\tilde{\alpha}(\infty)=z$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- definition-37: body_md -->
\label{ladder defn}
	Let ${\Sigma}$ be a $K_0$-qi section over $B$ in $X$, $z,z'\in \partial F_b$ such that $z\neq z'$. For each $s\in B$, let
 $z_s=\partial\phi^h_{bs}(z)$ and $z'_s=\partial \phi^h_{bs}(z')$, where $\phi_{bs}:F_b\to F_s$ be the fiber identification map.\\
 A {\bf semi-infinite ladder}, ${\mathbb L}({\Sigma},z)$, is the union of quasigeodesic rays in $\widehat{F}_s,s\in B$ joining ${\Sigma}\cap \widehat{F}_s$ to $z_s$ and a {\bf bi-infinite ladder}, ${\mathbb L}(z;z')$ is the union of quasigeodesic lines in $\widehat{F}_s,s\in B$ joining $z_s$ and $z'_s$.
 Both the ladders are contained in $\mathcal{X}$.
<!-- end definition-37 -->
<!-- lemma-50: body_md -->
\label{infinite ladder property}\cite[Lemma 6.14]{krishna-sardar}
	Suppose ${\mathbb L}$ is an infinite girth ladder. 
	\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=\parindent,align=left,labelwidth=\parindent,labelsep=4pt]
		\item There is a uniformly coarsely Lipschitz retraction $\Pi:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow {\mathbb L}$ such that for all $b\in B$ and $x\in \widehat{F}_b$, $\Pi(x)$ is an electric projection of $x$ in $\widehat{F}_b$ on ${\mathbb L}\cap \widehat{F}_b$.		
		\item Infinite girth ladders are uniformly quasiconvex and there exists $C>0$ such that a $C$-neighbourhood of the ladder is qi embedded in $\mathcal{X}$.
		\item Through any point of ${\mathbb L}$, there exists a $\bar{K}_0$-qi section contained in ${\mathbb L}$.
		\item Any qi section in ${\mathbb L}$ coarsely bisects it into two subladders.
		\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-50 -->
<!-- definition-38: body_md -->
$(1)$ Let $Z_1\subset Z_2$ be hyperbolic geodesic metric spaces such that the inclusion map $I:Z_1\to Z_2$ admits CT map, $\partial I:\partial Z_1\to\partial Z_2$. Then the {\bf Cannon-Thurston lamination} is given by $\ensuremath{\partial^{(2)}_{Z_2}}(Z_1)=\{(a,b)\in \partial^{(2)}Z_1:\partial I(a)=\partial I(b)\}$.\\
$(2)$ A (quasi)geodesic line $\alpha$ in $Z_1$ with $(\alpha(-\infty),\alpha(\infty))\in\ensuremath{\partial^{(2)}_{Z_2}}(Z_1)$ is called a {\bf leaf} of the CT lamination.\\
$(4)$ Let $Z\subset Z_1$ be a qi embedded subset. A leaf $\alpha\subset Z_1$ of $\ensuremath{\partial^{(2)}_{Z_2}}(Z_1)$ is said to be {\bf carried by $Z$} if $\alpha(\pm\infty)\in\partial Z$.
<!-- end definition-38 -->
<!-- lemma-51: body_md -->
\label{cor: asymptotic lifts}\cite[Lemma 6.19]{krishna-sardar}.
	Let ${\mathbb L}={\mathbb L}(z_1;z_2)$ for $(z_1,z_2)\in\partial^{(2)}_{\mathcal{X}}(\widehat{F})$.
	Let $\xi\in\partial B$ and $\beta:[0,\infty)\to B$ be a continuous, arc length parameterized $\kappa_0$-quasigeodesic in $B$. Then any two qi lifts of $\beta$ in ${\mathbb L}$ are asymptotic in $\mathcal{X}$.
<!-- end lemma-51 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{CT leaf in Y-0}
	Suppose we have a metric graph bundle satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{main theorem}. Suppose $\gamma$ is a quasigeodesic line in $\mathcal{Y}$ 
	such that $\gamma(\infty),\gamma(-\infty)$ are identified in $\partial\mathcal{X}$. Then $\gamma(\pm\infty)\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{Y}}(\widehat{F}_b)\setminus\bigcup_{\xi\in\partial A}\partial^{\xi}\mathcal{Y}$ for some (any) $b\in V(A)$.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{CT leaf in Y}
	Suppose we have a metric graph bundle satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{main theorem} such that $X$ is a proper metric space. Let $\gamma$ be a geodesic line in $Y^h$ with $\partial i_{Y,X}(\gamma(\infty))=\partial i_{Y,X}(\gamma(-\infty))$ in $\partial X^h$. Let $b\in V(A)$ and $F=F_b$. Then\\
	$(1)$ $\gamma(\pm\infty)\in\partial i_{F,Y}(\partial F^h)$.\\	
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
	$(2)$                               
	There exists a uniform quasigeodesic line $\sigma$ in $F^h$ at a finite Hausdorff distance from $\gamma$, in $Y^h$, satisfying $\partial i_{F,Y}(\sigma(\pm\infty))=\gamma(\pm\infty)$.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Throughout the proof, by Lemmas \ref{hamenstadt} and \ref{all boundaries}, we identify each non-parabolic point of $\partial X^h$ (resp. $\partial Y^h$) with the corresponding point in $\partial\mathcal{X}$ (resp. $\partial\mathcal{Y}$).
We first note that both $\gamma(\pm\infty)$ cannot be parabolic limit points in $\partial Y^h$, since each fiber is embedded in $Y$ and $X$ by a uniform type preserving map. \\
{\bf Case 1.} Suppose $\partial i_{Y,X}(\gamma(\pm\infty))$ is non-parabolic in $\partial X^h$. Then both $\gamma(\pm\infty)$ are non-parabolic limit points. Identifying them with the boundary points in $\partial\mathcal{Y}$, and applying Theorem \ref{CT leaf in Y-0}, we have that $\gamma(\pm\infty)\in\Lambda_{\mathcal{Y}}(\widehat{F})$, and again by Lemma \ref{hamenstadt}, $\gamma(\pm\infty)\in\Lambda_{Y^h}(F^h)$. As $F^h$ is proper, by Lemma \ref{CT-limset}, $\gamma(\pm\infty)\in\partial i_{F,Y}(\partial F^h)$.

\medskip
\noindent
We prove $(2)$ in this case. This part is very similar to that in \cite[Theorem 6.25]{krishna-sardar} Let $\sigma:{\mathbb R}\to F^h$ be a geodesic line such that $\partial i_{b,Y}(\sigma(\pm\infty))=\gamma(\pm\infty)$. 
Let $\{a_n^{\pm}\}$ be a sequence of points in $\sigma((0,\pm\infty))\cap F$ such that $a_n^{\pm}\to\sigma(\pm\infty)$ in $F^h$. Suppose $a_n^{\pm}\to z_{\pm}$ in $\widehat{F}$.
Let ${\mathbb L}={\mathbb L}(z_+;z_-)$ and $\Sigma_{\pm n}$ be a $\bar{K}_0$-qi section in ${\mathbb L}$ passing through $a_n^{\pm}$, $n\in {\mathbb N}$. Let $\alpha$ be a geodesic ray in $B$ with $\alpha(0)=b$ and $\alpha(\infty)=\xi$. Let $\tilde{\alpha}_{\pm n}$ be a qi lift of $\alpha$ in ${\Sigma}_{\pm n}$. By Corollary~\ref{cor: asymptotic lifts}, $\tilde{\alpha}_{\pm n}$'s are asymptotic. Also, these are $\bar{K}_0$-quasigeodesics. Recall that by Lemma~\ref{ideal triangles are slim}, the ideal triangle $\tilde{\alpha}_n\cup\tilde{\alpha}_{-n}\cup[a^+_n,a^-_n]_{\mathcal{X}}$ is $R=D_{\ref{ideal triangles are slim} }(\delta,\bar{K}_0)$-slim. So, there exists $t_n\geq 0$ such that $\tilde{\alpha}_n(t_n)\in N_R(\tilde{\alpha}_{-n})$ and $\tilde{\alpha}_{-n}(t_n)\in N_R(\tilde{\alpha}_n)$ (as long as $\tilde{\alpha}_n(t_n)$ and
$\tilde{\alpha}_{-n}(t_n)$ are not contained in the $R$-neighborhood of $[a^+_n,a^-_n]_{\mathcal{X}}$). This further implies that $d_{\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\alpha}_n(t_n),\tilde{\alpha}_{-n}(t_n))\leq R+\bar{K}_0R+\bar{K}_0$.\\
Let $R_2=\max\{R+\bar{K}_0R+\bar{K}_0,M_{\bar{K}_0}\}$.
Thus for all $n\in{\mathbb N}$, $U_{n}=U_{R_2}({\Sigma}_n, {\Sigma}_{-n})\neq \emptyset$. Let ${\mathbb L}_n={\mathbb L}({\Sigma}_n,{\Sigma}_{-n})$. Let $b_n$ be a nearest point projection of $b$ on $U_n$ and let $b'_n$ be a nearest point projection of $b_n$ on $A$. Let $\beta_n=[b,b'_n]$.
Then $\bar{c}_n=\bar{c}(a^+_n,a^-_n)$ is formed by the concatenation of the lifts $\tilde{\beta}_{\pm n}$ in ${\Sigma}_{\pm n}$ and $\widehat{F}_{b'_n}\cap{\mathbb L}_n$. This is a uniform quasigeodesic in $\mathcal{Y}$. Let $p\in F$. Let $\eta_n$ be hyperbolic geodesics in $Y^h$ joining $a^+_n,a^-_n$.

By Lemma~\ref{convergence explained}, there exists $M>0$ such that $d_{Y^h}(p,\tilde{\eta}_n)\leq M$ for all $n>0$. For all $n>0$, by Lemma~\ref{lemma from limint}, $d_Y(p,\tilde{\eta}_n\cap Y)\leq K_{\ref{lemma from limint}}(M)$ and by Lemma~\ref{hyp-pel-track}, $d_Y(p,\tilde{c}_n\cap Y)\leq K_{\ref{lemma from limint}}(M)+C$. Let $D=K_{\ref{lemma from limint}}(M)+C$. Then, $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(p,\tilde{c}_n\cap Y)\leq D$ for all $n>0$. But as $n\to\infty$, $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(p,a^{\pm}_n)\to\infty$ implies that $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(p,\tilde{\beta}_{\pm n})\to\infty$. So,  \begin{equation*}
	d_{\mathcal{Y}}(p,F_{b'_n}\cap{\mathbb L}_n)\leq D \text{ for large enough }n.
\end{equation*}
For $n>0$, let $\sigma_n=\widehat{F}\cap{\mathbb L}_n$. We first show that $\sigma_n$ is a uniform quasigeodesic in $\mathcal{Y}$.\\ 
Since $\sigma_n$ is a geodesic in $\widehat{F}$, it is uniformly coarsely Lipschitz and properly embedded in $\mathcal{Y}$. By Proposition~\ref{ladders are qi embedded}(2), $Hd_{\mathcal{Y}}(\sigma_n,\bar{c}_n)$ is uniformly bounded. So by Lemma~\ref{quasigeod criteria}, $\sigma_n$ is a uniform quasigeodesic in $\mathcal{Y}$. Let $\sigma^h_n$ be a hyperbolic geodesic in $Y^h$ with endpoints $a^+_n,a^-_n$. Then $Hd_Y(\sigma_n\cap Y,\sigma^h_n\cap Y)$ is uniformly small and $\sigma_n\cap F$ lies in a uniform neighbourhood of $\sigma\cap F$ in $F$. So, $\sigma^h_n$ lies in a uniform neighbourhood of $\sigma$ in $Y^h$. As $a^{\pm}_n\to\infty$, since $Y^h$ is proper, $\sigma^h_n$ converges to a hyperbolic geodesic line in $Y^h$, which is uniformly Hausdorff close to $\sigma$. Again by Lemma~\ref{quasigeod criteria}, $\sigma$ is a quasigeodesic line in $Y^h$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                              
 
          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                            

\noindent
{\bf Case 2. }Now suppose $\partial i_{Y,X}(\gamma(\pm\infty))$ is a parabolic limit point in $\partial X^h$. Let $\partial i_{Y,X}(\gamma(\pm\infty))=\Lambda({\mathcal C}_{\alpha}^h)$, where ${\mathcal C}_{\alpha}\in{\mathcal C}$. Denote by ${\mathcal C}_{Y,\alpha}={\mathcal C}_{\alpha}\cap Y$.\\
{\bf Case 2.1. } Suppose $\gamma(\infty)$ is a non-parabolic limit point of $\partial Y^h$ and $\gamma(-\infty)$ is a parabolic limit point. Let $\gamma(\infty)\in\partial^{\xi}{\mathcal{Y}}$ for some $\xi\in\partial A$. Let $\beta_1:[0,\infty)\to A$ be a geodesic ray with $\beta_1(0)=b,\beta_1(\infty)=\xi$ and $\tilde{\beta}_1$ be a qi lift in $\mathcal{Y}$ such that $\tilde{\beta}_1(\infty)=\gamma(\infty)$ in $\partial^{\xi}{\mathcal{Y}}$. Let $\tilde{\beta}_2\subset{\mathcal C}_{Y,\alpha}$ be a qi lift of $\beta$ in $\mathcal{Y}$. Then $\partial i_{\mathcal{Y},\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\beta}_1(\infty)) =\partial i_{\mathcal{Y},\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\beta}_2(\infty))\in\Lambda{\mathcal C}_{\alpha}$ and this implies that $Hd_{\mathcal{X}}(\tilde{\beta}_1,\tilde{\beta}_2)<\infty$ and as $\mathcal{Y}$ is properly embedded in $\mathcal{X}$, $Hd_{\mathcal{Y}}(\tilde{\beta}_1,\tilde{\beta}_2)<\infty$. This gives a contradiction. Therefore, $\gamma(\infty)\in\partial i_{F,Y}({\partial{F^h}})$.\\
Let $z_1,z_2\in\partial F^h$ such that $\partial i_{F,Y}(z_1)=\gamma(\infty)$ and $\partial i_{\widehat{F},\mathcal{Y}}(z_2)=\gamma(-\infty)$. We know that for $z_2=\Lambda H_{b,\alpha}^h$, $\partial i(z_2)=\Lambda({\mathcal C}_{\alpha}^h)$. We consider this case first. \\
{\bf Case 2.1.1.} $z_2=\Lambda H_{b,\alpha}^h$. Let $\sigma:{\mathbb R}\to F^h$ be a geodesic line with $\sigma(\infty)=z_1$ and $\sigma(-\infty)=z_2$. Let $a\in H_{b,\alpha}$ be the point where $\sigma$ enters $H_{b,\alpha}^h$. Let $\Sigma$ be a qi section in $\mathcal{X}$, through $a$, lying in ${\mathcal C}_{\alpha}$. Without loss of generality, let $\{a_n\}\subset\sigma\cap F$ such that $a_n\to z_1$ in $F^h$. Identifying $z_1\in\partial\widehat{F}$, we know that $\partial i_{\widehat{F},\mathcal{X}}(z_1)\in\Lambda({\mathcal B}_{\alpha})$ in $\partial \mathcal{X}$ (see Lemma \ref{hamenstadt}, Remark \ref{remark about bdry} and Lemma \ref{all boundaries}). Since ${\mathcal B}_{\alpha}$ is an isometric embedding, there exists $\xi\in\partial B$ such that $i_{\widehat{F},\mathcal{X}}(z_1)=\Lambda({\mathcal B}_{\alpha})\cap\partial^{\xi}\mathcal{X}$. Consider ${\mathbb L}={\mathbb L}(\Sigma,z_1)$. Let ${\Sigma}_n$ be a $\bar{K}_0$-qi section in ${\mathbb L}$ passing through $a_n$. Let $\beta$ be a geodesic ray in $B$ with $\beta(0)=b$ and $\beta(\infty)=\xi$. Let $\tilde{\beta},\tilde{\beta}_n$ be qi lift of $\beta$ in ${\Sigma},{\Sigma}_{n}$ for each $n$, respectively. By Corollary~\ref{cor: asymptotic lifts}, $\tilde{\beta}_n$ and $\tilde{\beta}$ are asymptotic and are $\bar{K}_0$-quasigeodesics. Putting $a^-_n=a$ for all $n>0$ and $a^+_n=a_n$ for all $n$, and taking $\tilde{\alpha}_{-n}$ (resp. ${\Sigma}_{-n}$) to be $\tilde{\beta}$ (resp. ${\Sigma}$) for all $n>0$, $\tilde{\alpha}_{+n}$ (resp. ${\Sigma}_{+n}$) to be $\tilde{\beta}_n$ (resp. ${\Sigma}_n$)  we repeat the steps of $(2)$ of Case 1.  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                
                
                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
Then, the subsegment of $\sigma$ starting at $a$ and limiting to $z_1$ is a hyperbolic quasigeodesic ray in $Y^h$ and further, by Lemma \ref{new quasigeodesic} and Lemma \ref{quasigeod criteria}, $\sigma$ itself is a quasigeodesic line in $Y^h$. \\
{\bf Case 2.1.2.} $z_2$ is a non-parabolic limit point of $F^h$. Let $z_0=\Lambda H_{b,\alpha}^h$. For $i=1,2$, let $\sigma_i$ be a geodesic line in $F^h$ with $\sigma_i(\infty)=z_i$ and $\sigma_i(-\infty)=z_0$. Applying Case 2.1.1 for the pairs $(z_0,z_1)$ and $(z_0,z_2)$, we have that $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ are quasigeodesic lines in $Y^h$. Since ideal (quasi)geodesic triangles of $F^h$ (resp. $Y^h$) are slim and by Lemma \ref{quasigeod criteria}, a fiber geodesic line $\sigma$ of $F^h$, with endpoints $z_1,z_2$, is a quasigeodesic line in $Y^h$.\\
{\bf Case 2.2.} Suppose $\gamma(\pm\infty)$ are both non-parabolic limit points of $\partial Y^h$. Let $x_0=\Lambda({\mathcal C}_{Y,\alpha}^h)$. Applying Case 2.1 to the pairs $(\gamma(\infty),x_0)$ and $(\gamma(-\infty),x_0)$, we have that $(\gamma(\pm\infty))\in\partial i_{F,Y}(\partial F^h)$. Let $z_1,z_2\in\partial F^h$ such that $\partial i_{F,Y}(z_1)=\gamma(\infty)$ and $\partial i_{F,Y}(z_2)=\gamma(-\infty)$. Then $z_1,z_2$ are non-parabolic limit points of $\partial F^h$ that are mapped to $\Lambda({\mathcal C}_{\alpha}^h)$ in $\partial X^h$. Then applying Case 2.1.2, we have that a geodesic line in $F^h$ joining $z_1,z_2$ is a quasigeodesic line in $Y^h$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lemma-52: body_md -->
\label{trasitive closure}
	$\ensuremath{\partial^{(2)}_{X}}(F)=\displaystyle{\big(\cup_{\xi\in\partial B}\ensuremath{\partial^{(2)}_{\xi}}(F)\big)^*}$.
<!-- end lemma-52 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:CT surjective}
	Suppose we have the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{main theorem} such that the fibers of the bundle are proper metric spaces. 
	Let $b\in A$. Suppose the CT map 
	$\partial i:\partial F_b^h\to\partial X^h$ is surjective. Then the CT map $\partial i_Y:\partial F_b^h\to\partial Y^h$ is also surjective.
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Let $\partial i_{Y,X}:\partial Y^h\to\partial X^h$ denote the CT map of the pullback.
Let $z\in \partial Y^h$. Since $\partial i$ is surjective,
there exists $z_1\in\partial F_b^h$ such that $\partial i(z_1)=\partial i_{Y,X}(z)$. Suppose $\partial i_Y(z_1)\neq z$.
Then, $\partial i_Y(z_1)$ and $z$ are elements of $\partial Y^h$ identified under $\partial i_{Y,X}$. Then by Theorem~\ref{CT leaf in Y}(1), there exists $z_2\in\partial F_b^h\setminus\{z_1\}$ such that $\partial i_Y(z_2)=z$. Therefore, we are done.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
Suppose $1\to (K,K_1)\to (G,N_G(K_1))\to (Q,Q_1)\to 1$ is a short exact sequence as in Theorem~\ref{combi for short exact seqn}. Suppose $Q'< Q$ is qi embedded and $G_1=\pi^{-1}(Q')$. 
	Then the CT map $\partial K^h\to\partial G_1^h$ is surjective.
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 1.1]{mj-rafi}\label{alg qc mjrafi}
Let $1\to K\to G\stackrel{\pi}{\to} Q\to 1$ be a short exact sequence of hyperbolic groups, where $K$ is a (closed) surface group or a free group and $Q$ is convex cocompact in Teichmuller space or outer space respectively. Let $H<K$ be a  finitely generated infinite index subgroup of $K$. Then $H$ is a quasiconvex subgroup in $G$.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 1.3]{mj-rafi}\label{alg rqc mjrafi}
Let $K=\pi_1(S^h)$ be the fundamental group of a surface with finitely many punctures and let $K_1,\ldots,K_n$ be its peripheral subgroups. Let $1\to K\to G\stackrel{\pi}{\to} Q\to1$ and $1\to K_i\to N_G(K_i)\stackrel{\pi}{\to}Q\to 1$ be the induced short exact sequences of groups. Suppose $Q$ is a convex cocompact subgroup of the pure mapping class group of $S^h$. Let $K'<K$ be a finitely generated infinite index subgroup of $K$. Then $K'$ is a relatively quasiconvex subgroup of $G$.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 4.3]{sardar-mj}\label{alg qc mjsardar}
Let $Q_1<Q$ be a quasiconvex subgroup of $Q$ and $G_1=\pi^{-1}(Q_1)$. Let $H_1<G_1$ be an infinite index quasiconvex subgroup of $G_1$. Then $H_1$ is quasiconvex in $G$.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- prop-14: body_md -->
\cite[Proposition 2.8]{sardar-mj}\label{prop from ms}
Let $G$ be a finitely presented group, $H,K<G$, where $H$ is finitely generated. Let $\Gamma=\Gamma(G,S)$ and $\Gamma_1=\Gamma(H,S_1)$ be the Cayley graphs, where $S,S_1$ are finite generating sets of $G,H$ respectively. Let $D>0$ and $A\subset N_D(K)\cap H$ be an infinite subset. Suppose there exists $r\geq 1$ such that any pair of points in $A$ can be joined by a path which lies in an $r$-neighbourhood of $A$ in $\Gamma_1$. Then there exists a finitely generated infinite subgroup $K'\subset H\cap K$ such that $A/K'$ is finite. In particular, $A$ is contained in a finite neighbourhood of $K'$ in $\Gamma$.
<!-- end prop-14 -->
<!-- convention-7: body_md -->
Let $G$ be a group hyperbolic relative to a collection of subgroups and let $H$ be a relatively hyperbolic subgroup such that the inclusion admits CT. We denote the CT lamination $\ensuremath{\partial^{(2)}_{G^h}}H^h$ simply by $\ensuremath{\partial^{(2)}_{G}}H$.
<!-- end convention-7 -->
<!-- lemma-53: body_md -->
\label{qc iff lam}\cite[Lemma 3.5]{mj-rafi}
Let $(G,{\mathcal H})$ be a relatively hyperbolic group and $(H,{\mathcal H}')$ be a relatively hyperbolic subgroup such that $(H,{\mathcal H}')\to(G,{\mathcal H})$ admits CT. Then $H$ is relatively quasiconvex in $G$ if and only if $\partial^{(2)}_G(H)=\emptyset$.
<!-- end lemma-53 -->
<!-- lemma-54: body_md -->
\label{lams}\cite{mitraonss}
Let $(G,{\mathcal H})$ be a relatively hyperbolic group and $(H_1,{\mathcal H}_1)$ and $(H_2,{\mathcal H}_2)$ be relatively hyperbolic subgroups such that $H_2<H_1$ and $(H_2,{\mathcal H}_2)\stackrel{i}{\to}(H_1,{\mathcal H}_1)$ and $(H_1,{\mathcal H}_1)\stackrel{j}{\to}(G,{\mathcal H})$ admit CT map. Then $\partial^{(2)}_G(H_2)=\partial^{(2)}_{H_1}(H_2)\cup\partial i^{-1}(\partial^{(2)}_{G}(H_1))$.
<!-- end lemma-54 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
Let ${\mathcal K}=\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n,{\mathcal H}=\{N_G(K_i)\}_{i=1}^n$. Let $$1\to (K,{\mathcal K})\to (G,{\mathcal H})\stackrel{\pi}{\to} (Q,Q)\to 1$$ be a short exact sequence of relatively hyperbolic groups. Let  $Q_1<Q$ be a quasiconvex subgroup of $Q$ and let $\pi^{-1}(Q_1)=G_1$. Suppose $H$ is an infinite index relatively quasiconvex subgroup of $G_1$. If $H$ is not relatively quasiconvex in $G$, then there exists an infinite index relatively quasiconvex subgroup of $K$ which is not relatively quasiconvex in $G$.
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Since $H$ is not relatively quasiconvex in $G$, by Lemma \ref{qc iff lam}, $\partial^{(2)}_G(H)\neq\emptyset$. Let $\gamma$ be a leaf of $\partial^{(2)}_G(H)$. Since $H$ is relatively quasiconvex in $G_1$, $\gamma$ is a leaf of $\partial^{(2)}_G(G_1)$. By Theorem \ref{CT leaf in Y}, there exists some $D'>0$ such that $\gamma$ lies in a $D'$-neighbourhood of $\Gamma_K^h$, where $\Gamma_K$ is the Cayley graph of $K$. Moreover, $\gamma(\pm\infty)$ are non-parabolic limit points of $\partial K^h$ as well as $\partial H^h$. This implies that there exists some $D>0$ such that $\gamma\cap H$ is an infinite subset lying in $N_D(K)\cap H$. By Proposition~\ref{prop from ms}, there exists a finitely generated infinite subgroup $K'\subset H\cap K$ and $R>0$ such that $\gamma\cap H$ lies in an $R$-neighbourhood of $K'$ in $\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is a Cayley graph of $G$. This implies that $\gamma(\pm\infty)\in\Lambda_H(K')$.\\
	{\bf Claim 1:} $[K:K']=\infty$. Suppose not. Then $\Lambda_K(K')=\partial K$. Since $\Lambda_{G_1}(K)=\partial G_1$, we have that $\Lambda_{G_1}(K')=\partial G_1$. Now, note that $\Lambda_{G_1}(K')\subset\Lambda_{G_1}(H)$. This will imply that $\Lambda_{G_1}(H)=\partial G_1$, which is a contradiction. \\
	{\bf Claim 2:} $K'$ is not relatively quasiconvex in $G$. Suppose not. Then $\partial^{(2)}_G(K')=\emptyset$ and by Lemma~\ref{lams}, $\partial^{(2)}_H(K')=\emptyset$.  Now, by Lemma \ref{qc iff lam}, $\partial^{(2)}_G(H)\neq\emptyset$ and for any leaf $\gamma$ of $\partial^{(2)}_G(H)$, $(\gamma(-\infty),\gamma(\infty))\in\partial^{(2)}_G(K')$. This is a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{ct lam rqc}
	Let $Q_1<Q$ be a quasiconvex subgroup of $Q$ and let $\pi^{-1}(Q_1)=G_1$. Then any infinite index relatively quasiconvex subgroup of $G_1$ is a relatively quasiconvex subgroup of $G$.
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
